'''Björn Sandstede''' is a German applied mathematician. He is currently the Alumni-Alumnae University Professor of Applied Mathematics at [[Brown University]], where he serves as chair of the department.<ref>[https://www.brown.edu/academics/applied-mathematics/people/faculty Faculty listing], Division of Applied Mathematics, Brown University, retrieved 2015-05-21.</ref> 

Sandstede earned his [[Dr. rer. nat.]] in 1993 from the [[University of Stuttgart]], under the supervision of [[Bernold Fiedler]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=27550}}</ref>

In 2001 he was awarded the [[J.D. Crawford Prize]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] for outstanding research in [[nonlinear science]].<ref name="SIAM">{{cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/crawford.php|title=J.D. Crawford Prize|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]|access-date=20 May 2015}}</ref> In 2014 Sandstede was awarded the Jack K. Hale Award for his contributions to partial differential equations and the study of spiral waves in reaction diffusion systems.<ref name="hale">[http://www.journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-differential-equations/news/inaugural-winner-of-elsevier-jack-k-hale-award/ Inaugural winner of Elsevier Jack K. Hale Award]</ref> He was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]], in the 2025 class of fellows.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2025|title=2025 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2024-11-01}}</ref>
